caption:
AI agents website checklist: 4 things Black-owned businesses should spell out now that AI shops and books for customers.

On November 4, 2026, Microsoft said AI agents now visit websites to shop and book for real people. Its free Microsoft Clarity tool found weekly visits from these agents nearly doubled in three weeks, to almost 2 million. Microsoft also added a test that checks whether an agent can finish a task on your site.

Make sure your website says, in plain text:
1. Exactly what you sell or the services you offer.
2. Your prices, or at least a clear starting price.
3. Your hours and where to find you.
4. How to book or buy, in as few steps as possible.

The easier your site is to read, the easier it is for anyone, human or AI, to choose you.

Microsoft says AI agents are now visiting small business websites to shop and book for people, and Black-owned businesses should get ready.

On November 4, 2026, Microsoft Clarity reported that weekly visits from AI agents nearly doubled in three weeks, to almost 2 million. It also added a test to check whether an agent can finish a task on a website.

When an AI is doing the shopping, clear words on your site matter as much as good photos. Prices, hours and booking steps should be easy to find.

caption_drafts.provocation:
Small business owners, could an AI book an appointment on your website right now? Microsoft just showed Black-owned businesses why that question matters.

On November 4, 2026, Microsoft said AI agents now visit websites to shop and book for people, and weekly agent visits nearly doubled in three weeks.

Picture two salons. One lists its services, prices and a booking link in plain words. The other hides everything in a flyer image. Only one of them is easy for anyone to read.
